questions.q: What does "shifting left" mean on a software delivery timeline?
options: Moving security activities earlier, toward planning and coding rather than release
Moving the release date earlier regardless of testing
Removing the operations team from the deployment process
Running security scans only after a production incident
questions.explain: On a timeline drawn left to right (plan, code, build, test, deploy, operate), shifting left means moving security checks toward the earlier, left-hand stages.

questions.q: Why is the same vulnerability more expensive to fix in production than in the editor?
options: Production code is written in a different language
The flaw itself changes and becomes more complex over time
Catching it later means incident response, pressure, and larger blast radius instead of a quick edit
Editors cannot detect any security issues at all
questions.explain: The flaw is identical — what changes is the cost and risk of discovery. A flaw caught while typing costs seconds; the same flaw found live can trigger an incident.

questions.q: How does DevSecOps extend the DevOps idea?
options: By replacing developers with dedicated security engineers
By embedding automated security checks directly into the same pipeline developers and operators already share
By moving all security work to a separate team performed after release
By eliminating the need for code review
questions.explain: DevSecOps weaves security checks into the existing DevOps pipeline so guardrails run automatically on every commit, rather than depending on a separate, later-stage review.

questions.q: Which best distinguishes SecOps from DevSecOps?
options: SecOps and DevSecOps are the same practice with different names
SecOps focuses on monitoring and responding to threats against running systems; DevSecOps embeds security checks into the build/release pipeline itself
SecOps only applies to cloud infrastructure, DevSecOps only to on-premises systems
DevSecOps replaces the need for any operations monitoring
questions.explain: SecOps is the operational, production-facing side of security (monitoring, detection, response). DevSecOps is about building security checks into the pipeline earlier in the lifecycle.

questions.q: In this course's framing, does shifting left make Northbridge Retail invulnerable to security incidents?
options: Yes, shifting left guarantees zero production incidents
No — it reduces risk and lowers the cost of catching flaws early, but incident response is still covered later in the course
Shifting left only applies to on-premises software, not cloud retailers
Shifting left eliminates the need for any identity or access controls
questions.explain: Shifting left lowers risk by catching issues earlier and cheaper — it does not eliminate risk entirely, which is why the course still covers incident response in Chapter 6.
